errors.evidence: The y-axis range extends below 50 (down to ~45 for LlamaGuard 1) and above 90 (up to ~97 for OmniGuard). Stating the range is 50 to 90 is incorrect.
The AegisGuard (P) line does not have cross markers. It has error bars, and the data points are marked with small circles.
The AegisGuard (P) line starts at an accuracy of approximately 52% for 0 few-shot examples, not 70%.

errors.text_span: decreases to about 53% across the x-axis range
errors.evidence: This description is an oversimplification. The AegisGuard (P) line first increases sharply from ~52% to a peak of ~77% at 1 few-shot example, before decreasing.
The AegisGuard (D) line does not have plus sign markers. It has error bars, and the data points are marked with small circles.
The LlamaGuard 1 line does not have square markers. It has error bars, and the data points are marked with small circles.

errors.text_span: remains relatively stable around 50% across the x-axis
errors.evidence: This is an oversimplification. While the LlamaGuard 1 line is near 50% for the first few points, it shows a clear downward trend after 3 examples, dropping to approximately 46% at 5 examples.
The markers for the LlamaGuard 2 line are squares, not diamonds.
The DuoGuard line does not have triangle markers. It has error bars, and the data points are marked with small circles.
The DuoGuard line begins at an accuracy of 70% for 0 few-shot examples, not 50%. It drops to 50% at 1 few-shot example.

errors.text_span: with all lines having error bars
errors.evidence: This statement is incorrect as the OmniGuard (black) line does not have any visible error bars.
